speaker.name: Liora
style_phrases: ends with 'And that's how it was.'
colour_lines: The harbor-master's lamp burns until the last boat is in, and goes out the moment it is.
The Tidewatch Lamp Room keeps odd hours, so knock twice, wait, and do not take it personally.
Most of what is said about the giant weasel is probably exaggerated, but not all of it.
own_lines: I was grown up in a trade caravan, never sleeping twice in the same bed.
I copied ledgers for a counting house. Numbers lie less than people do, though not by much.
I was caught at the edge of a border skirmish once and walked away without a scratch. I do not take that for granted.
My word is the one coin I carry that cannot be forged. I spend it carefully.
My old dog is waiting at home. He has opinions about how late I am getting back.
I want a small garden and a quiet chair. I have wanted them for years.

An old friend, Perrin, holds a sack of precious seed-grain for me.

Someone else wants it as badly as I do, and they have been watching my door.

Walk me there, and I'll make sure you're repaid.
Thank you for seeing me through.

exchanges.hero_words: Quit stalling. What do you want from us?
exchanges.reply: Listen, I need you to collect it from Perrin for me; my word is the one coin I carry that cannot be forged, so I spend it carefully. My old dog is waiting at home, and he has opinions about how late I’m getting back. And that’s how it was.
